title: pr-15803-onboard-orchid-11b-v1.0-performance-profiles-changelog-automation
author: Aisha Khan
ci_status: pass (tests rerun after flaky kv-cache test)
description:
Onboard Orchid-11B v1.0: add model metadata, performance profiles for common hardware targets, and wire up changelog/release-notes automation. Motivation: Orchid-11B is a community LLM with promising quality/cost tradeoffs. This PR registers the model in the registry, provides validated perf profiles (A100, T4 quantized, CPU int8 smoke), and updates automation so a changelog entry is generated when metadata or perf profiles change. Includes small infra to prevent regressions by failing CI if perf profile schema validation fails.

Checklist:
- [x] Add model metadata (name, architecture, tokenizer, download provenance, license)
- [x] Add performance profiles for A100-40GB, A10G, and T4 quantized 4-bit paths
- [x] Add smoke validation tests that run a short latency/throughput sweep on synthetic prompts
- [x] Add changelog automation mapping so updates to perf profiles generate a draft release note entry
- [x] Update onboarding docs snippet with recommended quantization + batching guidelines

What changed (high level):
- Registered model entry under models/orchid-11b/v1.0 with canonical metadata and checksums (sha256).
- Added perf profiles under perf_profiles/orchid-11b/v1.0/{a100,t4-4bit,a10g}-profile.json containing latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, recommended batch sizes, kv-cache hints, and quantization flags.
- Added tests/perf_smoke/orchid_11b_smoke_test.py which runs a short generation workload against the local perf harness (CI-friendly).
- Extended scripts/tools/changelog_generator to consume perf_profiles diffs and create a formatted release note entry under changelogs/drafts/.
- Added schema validation in ci/checks/perf_profile_lint.py to ensure new profiles match expected format and thresholds do not regress beyond allowed deltas.

Why this matters:
- Provides customers and internal teams a validated starting point for Orchid-11B on common deployment targets.
- Changelog automation reduces manual work and ensures perf changes are traceable in release notes.
- CI validation prevents accidental format regressions that previously led to runtime errors in the serving runtime.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for metadata parsing and schema validation included.
- CI runs perf_smoke tests using a canned local runtime image; flakiness observed in one kv-cache unit test was fixed by increasing timeout and retry (see commit 2).
- Manual spot checks on A100 and T4 quantized path showed p50 latency within expected bounds (A100 p50 ~ 42ms for 256-tokens; T4-4bit p50 ~ 210ms).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge into main.
2) Wait for nightly full perf sweep.
3) Publish changelog draft and notify release owner.
4) Tag as v1.0 in registry once release sign-off complete.

Notes: model weights are linked to an external s3 artifact (s3://redwood-models/orchid/11b/v1.0/) with access-limited presigned URLs for CI. License is MIT-compatible; see metadata.

References: Linear ENG-3421, internal evaluation notebook link: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-3421 (internal), model card template: docs/model-registry/ORCHID_MODEL_CARD.md
